units.function: Database service tests for instance-wide environment persistence, lease basics, deletion impact/guards, local/managed runtime provisioning, concurrency deduplication, managed stock drift and provider archive/reactivation.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest -> environment service -> Drizzle/embedded Postgres across environment, lease, company, Agent, workspace, issue/project, Secret binding, custom-image, managed-resource and activity tables; provider runtime and route authorization are not exercised.
units.keyDataModels: Instance environment and metadata markers, environment lease, instance default, cross-company selection/reference counts, built-in managed-resource stock hash/version/defaults, operator drift status and activity events.
units.lifecycle: Create/ensure one local or managed sandbox slot -> reconcile stock/provider availability while preserving operator drift -> acquire/release leases -> compute deletion blast radius -> atomically refuse local/default deletion or remove another row -> route layer later clears references.
units.testAssessment: Sandboxed and approved unsandboxed focused runs skipped 26/26 because embedded Postgres is unsupported. The source specifies valuable concurrency and reconciliation cases, but no database behavior is locally verified. Delete safety, lease races, tenant ownership and service-level invariant enforcement remain incomplete by design or coverage.
units.designRationale: Keep installation-managed execution infrastructure stable across concurrent boot, provider changes and stock upgrades while respecting operator modifications and exposing the impact of destructive removal.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs independent deployment-node and tenant-profile persistence, upgrade-safe managed defaults, explicit operator overrides, governed leases and deletion workflows across cloud and self-hosted profiles.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT the ownership/data model while adopting stock-hash/default snapshots, operator-drift classification, marker-backed hardened runtime selection and database uniqueness. Separate global deployment nodes from tenant grants/profiles; enforce all config invariants in the domain; make deletion a drain/approval/saga state machine that blocks on active use and references; use compare-and-set lease transitions and transactional outbox evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: Company context does not own the environment row, managed adoption can reclassify operator resources, and destructive removal is not bound to affected tenants or accountable humans. Blast-radius information is advisory rather than an enforced responsibility/approval contract.
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL tenant ownership gap: environment rows and managed slot uniqueness are instance-wide while company context lives in surrounding records. CRITICAL destructive-race gap: active leases/image setup and most references do not block atomic deletion. HIGH unverified database gap: all 26 tests skip locally. HIGH ownership-transfer gap: cloud boot can stamp an existing operator local row as platform managed. HIGH invariant gap: service create can persist configs that routes reject. HIGH lease concurrency/state-transition coverage gap.
